seo.og_title: Dragon Island, Dakhla: Boat Trips, Lagoon & Visitor Tips
seo.og_description: What to see and do at Dakhla's famous Dragon Island, from boat excursions across the turquoise lagoon to birdwatching.

name: Dragon Island
hero_subtitle: A rocky islet in the lagoon shaped like a sleeping dragon — boat, kayak or low-tide approach.

overview.title: Silhouette in the middle of the bay
overview.p1: Dragon Island (Île du Dragon) rises from the turquoise lagoon with a rocky ridge that, from the right angle, resembles a sleeping dragon resting in the water. It is one of Dakhla’s most iconic boat excursion destinations.
overview.p2: At low tide, shallow sandbars emerge around it, while high tide transforms it into a true island retreat ideal for small boats, zodiacs, and adventurous kayakers.
overview.p3: There are no permanent structures on the island. Bring water, sun protection, and respect the pristine nature and migratory bird life of the protected lagoon ecosystem.

2.title: Exploring the islet
2.desc: Walk along the shore, discover marine shells, and enjoy panoramic views from the ridge.

3.title: Return sail with scenic views
3.desc: Sail back across the bay as the afternoon sun casts a golden glow over the water.

food.title: Picnicking & Refreshments
food.p1: Because Dragon Island is an uninhabited and protected natural site, there are no restaurants or shops directly on the islet.
food.li1: Bring your own bottled water and hydrating drinks.
food.li2: Pack light snacks, energy bars, or a picnic if doing a full excursion.
food.li3: Many boat tours include a freshly prepared lunch or tea stop on nearby shores.
food.li4: Remember to pack out all your trash to keep the island pristine.
food.li5: Enjoy full dining options back at town restaurants or lagoon kite camps.
food.p2: Planning ahead ensures you stay comfortable throughout your boat or kayak adventure.

tips.title: Practical Tips for Visiting Dragon Island

1.title: Getting There
1.desc: Accessible via organized boat trips departing from local kite camps or hotels along the lagoon, or by renting a kayak if staying nearby.

2.title: Tides & Safety
2.desc: Check local tide schedules before planning a crossing. Strong currents can occur between the mainland and the island during tide changes.

3.title: What to Bring
3.desc: Water, sunscreen, sturdy footwear for walking on rocky shell beds, and waterproof bags for electronics during boat or kayak transfers.

q1.question: Is Dragon Island free to visit?
q1.answer: Yes, stepping onto the island is free, but you will need to arrange a boat, zodiac, or kayak excursion to cross the lagoon waters.

q2.question: What is the best time to go to Dragon Island?
q2.answer: Morning or early afternoon when the lagoon tide is right and wind conditions are calm for boat or kayak crossings.

q3.question: Why is it called Dragon Island?
q3.answer: Its elongated rocky ridge and silhouette viewed from above or afar resemble the shape of a sleeping dragon resting in the water.

q4.question: How long should I spend at Dragon Island?
q4.answer: Plan around 2 to 3 hours for the boat trip across the lagoon, walking around the islet, and exploring the shoreline.

q5.question: Can I see wildlife on Dragon Island?
q5.answer: Yes, the island and surrounding shallow waters are frequent feeding grounds for migratory birds and rich in marine shells.
